## Reviewed primary-source context

### DP World extends Luanda concession to 2051 and plans $90m expansion
Source date: 2026-10-06 | Review: 2026-10-06 | Stage at source date: Extension granted; expansion announced

- A 10-year extension takes the concession to 2051.
- DP World announced another $90 million of investment over two years.
- Planned terminal capacity is 1.2 million TEU.
- The expansion includes three ship-to-shore cranes and 12 semi-automated RTGs.

Source: [DP World](https://www.dpworld.com/en/news/dp-world-granted-extension-for-angolas-luanda-terminal-concession-to-2051-and-announces-us90-million-expansion)

Analytical interpretation: The extension adds contracted operating life, while new capex creates a cash outflow before capacity produces earnings. Model incremental demand and cash flow rather than treating design capacity as revenue.

Undisclosed / to verify: Capex phasing, Incremental contracted volume, Tariff assumptions, Financing mix, Handback requirements.

### EIB provides €100m for Klaipėda’s port transformation
Source date: 2026-09-15 | Review: 2026-10-06 | Stage at source date: Loan announced

- The EIB financing is €100 million.
- The overall project costs around €201 million.
- Works include shoreside electricity, hydrogen facilities and offshore wind infrastructure.

Source: [European Investment Bank](https://www.eib.org/en/press/all/2026-293-eib-helps-transform-lithuania-s-port-of-klaipeda-into-defence-and-clean-energy-hub-with-eur100-million-in-financing)

Analytical interpretation: Debt is a funding source, not the asset valuation. Test which cash flows repay the loan and how grants change the equity requirement.

Undisclosed / to verify: Interest rate, Maturity, Amortization, Revenue allocation.

### Partners Group’s secondaries strategy returns to atNorth
Source date: 2026-09-02 | Review: 2026-10-06 | Stage at source date: Around 10% investment announced

- Partners Group’s secondaries strategy will acquire around 10%.
- The prior sale to CPP Investments and Equinix valued the company at $4 billion enterprise value.
- The September release says the prior transaction has closed.

Source: [Partners Group](https://www.partnersgroup.com/en/news-and-views/press-releases/investment-news/detail?news_id=95eb4c3a-eae1-4ff3-9f64-10781dff63c0)

Analytical interpretation: Ten percent of enterprise value is not the price of 10% equity. Deduct net debt and review the capital structure and valuation date.

Undisclosed / to verify: New investment price, Current net debt, Growth capex obligations, Contracted versus operating EBITDA.

### Hapag-Lloyd agrees to acquire 25% of Maasvlakte II
Source date: 2026-08-19 | Review: 2026-10-06 | Stage at source date: Announced; approvals required

- Hapag-Lloyd is to acquire a 25% stake.
- Completion is subject to relevant authority and regulatory approvals.
- Financial terms were not disclosed.

Source: [APM Terminals](https://akamai.apmterminals.com/en/news/news-releases/2026/260819-APMTerminals-and-Hapag-Lloyd-partner-at-Maasvlakte-II)

Analytical interpretation: A shipping line buying terminal equity may improve network access. Examine minority protections and whether volume commitments create measurable value.

Undisclosed / to verify: Purchase price, Net debt, EBITDA, Shareholder protections.

### DP World plans a €48m cold-chain hub in Antwerp
Source date: 2026-08-05 | Review: 2026-10-06 | Stage at source date: Announced project

- Initial investment is €48 million.
- Later phases could bring long-term investment to around €100 million.
- The planned site covers 83,000 square metres next to Antwerp Gateway.

Source: [DP World](https://www.dpworld.com/en/news/dp-world-expands-cold-chain-capabilities-with-new-48m-antwerp-hub)

Analytical interpretation: Compare initial spend with stabilized rent or logistics margin. Do not count the €48m and €100m as two separate deals.

Undisclosed / to verify: Occupancy commitments, Lease structure, Operating margin, Phase timing.
